replication.target_description: Primary report located; ambiguous online versus lab Study 1 perceived brightness tests; Study 2 watts also possible under broad outcome wording.

notes: Identity verified from cover and manuscript: matching title with replication/meta-analysis subtitle, authors Mark J. Brandt, Hans IJzerman, Irene Blanken, Social Psychology 45(3), 246–252 (2014), DOI 10.1027/1864-9335/a000191. Document labelled Peer reviewed version. This is a primary replication report, not the original Banerjee source. The supplied text contains manuscript pages 1–18, methods, results, tables and figure captions; Figures 2–3 plotted data are not represented in the text. No PDF supplied, so no rendering possible. Replication study identifier is null. The neutral description does not distinguish online from lab studies. Manuscript pp. 3–4 contain introduction/general methods, not unique replication results; correspondence to the supplied publication-page locators is not established. Even restricting to original Study 1 leaves two candidate replications. No target assigned by audit ID, input order, numeric matching or row counts. Assigned replication locator: p.4. Candidates only: Table 2, manuscript p. 15, Study 1 perceived brightness d = .12 online, -.11 lab; Study 2 estimated watts d = .05 online, .03 lab if the broad brightness description includes watts. Table 2 labels these d and documents use of Becker’s effect size calculator; no conversion performed. Superscript a/b letters in canonical rows label original-versus-replication effect comparisons. Table 2 p < .05 concerns differences between effect sizes, not the critical condition comparison. Results, manuscript p. 6, reports primary condition-test bounds collectively: online p >.20, lab p >.55. These are bounds, not exact p values. Table 1, manuscript p. 14, largest available study Ns: online Study 1 475, lab Study 1 100; online Study 2 482, lab Study 2 121. Participants, manuscript p. 5, expressly warns that missing measures change analytic samples. These are candidate study-level participant counts only, not established analytic N. No N derived from df, no group sum, exact-test exclusions unresolved. Original and reported_success are unassigned placeholders; do not overwrite verified fields.
